title: First solo letter
scenario: The first letter that appears exactly once.

intro.job: The first letter that appears exactly once.

model_restatement: Find the first letter in the word that occurs exactly once, and print it.

clarify.question: What if every letter repeats?
clarify.answer: Today there's always at least one solo letter.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each letter, check how many times it shows up in the whole word. The first letter that shows up exactly once is the answer — print it and stop.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after the counting loop finishes (iteration 5), what is counts?

why_line: The very first letter is never in an empty set, so the draft prints 's' straight away — before it has any idea that 's' comes back twice more.

explain.rule: Picking the first new face is calling 'only child!' at the first kid through the door — before her two brothers walk in.
explain.bridge: So what do you need to know about every letter before you can call one 'solo'?

fix.rule: Two passes: count everything first, then the first letter with count 1 is the answer.

walk.gloss: Pass one: every letter of the word.
Pass two: the first letter whose count is exactly 1 wins.

alternatives.note: word.count recounts for every letter — correct, but slow on long words.

hints: Iteration 1: is 's' in the empty set?
'Not seen yet' only means new SO FAR — 's' comes back later.
Count every letter first, then look for the first count of 1.

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — p repeats, so the first solo letter is a.

one_liner: Count the whole word first — the first letter you haven't seen yet isn't the first letter that appears once.

choices.label: One word — a string of letters
Every letter that shows up once
The first letter that shows up exactly once, printed
How many letters show up once

questions.prompt: In THIS word, which letter is the first to show up exactly once? Work it out by hand.
The first letter, s — is it the answer just because nothing came before it?

choices.label: Yes — it's first and nothing matched it yet
No — s shows up again later, so it isn't alone

hints: For each letter, ask how many times it shows up in the whole word.
word.count(ch) says how many times ch is in word — stop at the first letter where that's 1.

why.this_data: Your version re-reads the whole word for every letter: 5 letters → 25 looks.
why.real_size: With a 10,000-letter word that's 100 million looks. Let's count every letter once, then just look it up.

blocks.title: Count every letter once
blocks.teaches: counts[ch] = counts.get(ch, 0) + 1 adds one to that letter's count — starting from 0 the first time.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 2, after line 3: what is counts?

blocks.title: Stop at the first one
blocks.teaches: break leaves the loop right away — so only the FIRST match is printed.

checkpoints.prompt: There are two 8s. What gets printed?

blocks.title: Ask the counts
blocks.teaches: counts[ch] hands back how many times ch showed up; == 1 asks 'exactly once?'

blocks.title: Count it all, then look
blocks.teaches: Look only after the WHOLE word is counted — mid-count, a letter that repeats later still looks like it shows up once.

checkpoints.prompt: 'a' shows up twice in 'aba'. What gets printed?

hints: Which block showed what goes wrong if you look before the counting is done?
B1's line belongs in the first loop — every letter is counted before anything is looked up.
Order: B1's line in the first loop, then B4's lines in the second.
